# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 800
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/800
- **Title**: ci(release): ASC version-floor pre-check + AAB gate self-test (#798)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/issue-798` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +398
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-09-22T08:39:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-22T19:20:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #798.

Both tripwires from the #797 triage, fail-closed, naming the rule each protects.

## 1. ASC version-floor pre-check (testflight leg) — AC1/AC2/E1/E2/AC4

**Decision module** `flutter_app/fastlane/version_floor.rb` (the `appstore_preflight.rb` pattern: the lane fetches ASC facts, a dependency-free plain-ruby module decides → the whole matrix is testable without ASC):
- floor = max of **approved** versions only (`ACCEPTED` / `PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE` / `READY_FOR_SALE`) — in-review / TestFlight-only versions never raise it (they can still be rejected; the check must not block on them)
- `stamped ≤ floor` → named abort: *«stamped X ≤ approved Y — bump rule / one-version scheme broken (gh-785); refusing to spend build minutes on a guaranteed-rejected upload (iris 90062)»*
- **E2**: no approved versions → floor `0.0.0`, trivially passes, still markers
- garbage stamp → named abort instead of comparing wrong

**Wiring**: `build-mobile.yml` `build-ios` runs `fastlane ios assert_version_floor` as step 5 — before pub get (step 6), pods, certs, and the build (step 14): a violation costs **zero build minutes**. The lane reads the **same `BUILD_NAME` the build lane stamps** (`needs.version.outputs.version` — the pubspec → tag → version-job source #797 centralized).
- **E1**: ASC unreachable → exactly one retry, then fail-closed named error («cannot verify the version floor, refusing to build»)
- no ASC secrets → **named SKIP** (they're optional repo secrets; the upload leg skips too — nothing to guard), never silent
- **AC4**: the lane always logs `[gh-798] version-floor pre-check RAN: stamped=… approved_floor=… verdict=…` (and `SKIPPED` when skipping) — a silently-skipped check is visible in the daily report

**AC1/AC2 verified** by `flutter_app/fastlane/test/version_floor_test.rb` (10 checks, auto-picked-up by ci.yml's plain-ruby loop): AC1 below-floor abort incl. the exact #785 shape (`0.1.452` vs approved `1.0.0`), AC2 `1.0.453 > 1.0.452` passes, strict monotonicity (equal aborts), numeric compare (`1.0.9 ≤ 1.0.10`), E2, in-review-does-not-raise. Ran locally: `version_floor: 10 checks OK`.

## 2. AAB 16 KB-gate self-test — AC3/E3

- The gate moved out of build-mobile.yml into **`scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh`** — one source for the daily leg and the self-test, so they can't drift. Behavior byte-identical to #797's gate (same glob, same named verdict).
- **`.github/workflows/aab-gate-selftest.yml`**: PR-triggered on the workflow / gate script / checker paths (+ manual dispatch). Builds two fixtures and runs the **real script**:
  - (a) real 16 KB-aligned vendored `.so` at `base/lib/<abi>/` (AAB layout) → gate passes **and** the green marker must be present
  - (b) lib-less bundle → gate must fail **and** output must contain the named `::error:: expected native libs at base/lib/*/*.so …` verdict — catching a regression to an inherited/unlabeled exit code (the exact gh-786 class)
- The fixture is AAB-layout, so **any glob/layout regression fails case (a) red** — demonstrated locally: sed-regressing the glob back to `lib/*` makes the with-libs fixture fail with the named error.
- Local run against the fixtures: (a) `scanned 1, patched 0, failed 0` + green; (b) named failure, exit 1.

## Guards

`test/store_automation_guard_test.dart` gains a `release-train tripwires (gh-798)` group: floor step must stay **before** build prep in build-ios, the lane must keep using the tested module + the AC4 marker, the daily gate must run via the shared script, and the self-test workflow must trigger on gate-script PRs. (The dart guard suite couldn't run in this sandbox — pub cache is denied — so the pinned facts were verified with an equivalent ruby check; the suite runs in CI.)

**Non-goals respected:** the `1.0.<counter>` scheme itself is untouched; no release automation beyond the two tripwires.

# pr-800: ci(release): ASC version-floor pre-check + AAB gate self-test (#798)

## Description

Closes #798.

Both tripwires from the #797 triage, fail-closed, naming the rule each protects.

## 1. ASC version-floor pre-check (testflight leg) — AC1/AC2/E1/E2/AC4

**Decision module** `flutter_app/fastlane/version_floor.rb` (the `appstore_preflight.rb` pattern: the lane fetches ASC facts, a dependency-free plain-ruby module decides → the whole matrix is testable without ASC):
- floor = max of **approved** versions only (`ACCEPTED` / `PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE` / `READY_FOR_SALE`) — in-review / TestFlight-only versions never raise it (they can still be rejected; the check must not block on them)
- `stamped ≤ floor` → named abort: *«stamped X ≤ approved Y — bump rule / one-version scheme broken (gh-785); refusing to spend build minutes on a guaranteed-rejected upload (iris 90062)»*
- **E2**: no approved versions → floor `0.0.0`, trivially passes, still markers
- garbage stamp → named abort instead of comparing wrong

**Wiring**: `build-mobile.yml` `build-ios` runs `fastlane ios assert_version_floor` as step 5 — before pub get (step 6), pods, certs, and the build (step 14): a violation costs **zero build minutes**. The lane reads the **same `BUILD_NAME` the build lane stamps** (`needs.version.outputs.version` — the pubspec → tag → version-job source #797 centralized).
- **E1**: ASC unreachable → exactly one retry, then fail-closed named error («cannot verify the version floor, refusing to build»)
- no ASC secrets → **named SKIP** (they're optional repo secrets; the upload leg skips too — nothing to guard), never silent
- **AC4**: the lane always logs `[gh-798] version-floor pre-check RAN: stamped=… approved_floor=… verdict=…` (and `SKIPPED` when skipping) — a silently-skipped check is visible in the daily report

**AC1/AC2 verified** by `flutter_app/fastlane/test/version_floor_test.rb` (10 checks, auto-picked-up by ci.yml's plain-ruby loop): AC1 below-floor abort incl. the exact #785 shape (`0.1.452` vs approved `1.0.0`), AC2 `1.0.453 > 1.0.452` passes, strict monotonicity (equal aborts), numeric compare (`1.0.9 ≤ 1.0.10`), E2, in-review-does-not-raise. Ran locally: `version_floor: 10 checks OK`.

## 2. AAB 16 KB-gate self-test — AC3/E3

- The gate moved out of build-mobile.yml into **`scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh`** — one source for the daily leg and the self-test, so they can't drift. Behavior byte-identical to #797's gate (same glob, same named verdict).
- **`.github/workflows/aab-gate-selftest.yml`**: PR-triggered on the workflow / gate script / checker paths (+ manual dispatch). Builds two fixtures and runs the **real script**:
  - (a) real 16 KB-aligned vendored `.so` at `base/lib/<abi>/` (AAB layout) → gate passes **and** the green marker must be present
  - (b) lib-less bundle → gate must fail **and** output must contain the named `::error:: expected native libs at base/lib/*/*.so …` verdict — catching a regression to an inherited/unlabeled exit code (the exact gh-786 class)
- The fixture is AAB-layout, so **any glob/layout regression fails case (a) red** — demonstrated locally: sed-regressing the glob back to `lib/*` makes the with-libs fixture fail with the named error.
- Local run against the fixtures: (a) `scanned 1, patched 0, failed 0` + green; (b) named failure, exit 1.

## Guards

`test/store_automation_guard_test.dart` gains a `release-train tripwires (gh-798)` group: floor step must stay **before** build prep in build-ios, the lane must keep using the tested module + the AC4 marker, the daily gate must run via the shared script, and the self-test workflow must trigger on gate-script PRs. (The dart guard suite couldn't run in this sandbox — pub cache is denied — so the pinned facts were verified with an equivalent ruby check; the suite runs in CI.)

**Non-goals respected:** the `1.0.<counter>` scheme itself is untouched; no release automation beyond the two tripwires.

+# never executes the checks.

+
+if $PROGRAM_NAME == __FILE__
+  $checks = 0
+
+  def ok(message)
+    $checks += 1
+    puts "  ok: #{message}"

+

+  ok("ACCEPTED/PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE count as approved")
+
+  # Numeric comparison, not string: 1.0.9 < 1.0.10

+  raise "FAIL: numeric compare broken, got #{d.inspect}" unless d["action"] == "abort" && d["floor"] == "1.0.10"
+  ok("numeric compare: 1.0.9 ≤ 1.0.10 aborts")
+
+  # Garbage stamp aborts named instead of comparing wrong
+  d = VersionFloor.decide(stamped: "auto", approved: [approved("1.0.0")])
+  raise "FAIL: garbage stamp must abort named, got #{d.inspect}" unless d["action"] == "abort" && d["reason"].include?("not a comparable")
+  ok("garbage stamp → named abort")
+
+  puts "version_floor: #{$checks} checks OK"
+end

index 00000000..6fc37521
--- /dev/null
+++ b/flutter_app/fastlane/version_floor.rb
@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+# frozen_string_literal: true
+
+# Pure decision logic for the TestFlight version-floor pre-check (issue
+# #798, triage of #785): the daily leg must abort BEFORE any build when the
+# version it is about to stamp is not strictly above the latest version App
+# Store Connect has already APPROVED (iris-code 90062 — a 20-minute build
+# ending in altool rejection is the failure class this kills). Dependency-
+# free — no fastlane/spaceship requires: the Fastfile lane fetches the ASC
+# facts, this module decides, so the whole matrix is testable with plain
+# ruby (test/version_floor_test.rb — no gems needed).
+module VersionFloor
+  # App Store states where Apple has APPROVED the version — only these
+  # raise the floor Apple's monotonicity check (90062) compares against.
+  # A version that merely exists as a TestFlight build or sits in review
+  # never counts: it can still be rejected, and the check must not block
+  # on it.
+  APPROVED_STATES = %w[
+    ACCEPTED
+    PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE
+    READY_FOR_SALE
+  ].freeze
+
+  # stamped:  the version the leg is about to stamp — BUILD_NAME, the same
+  #           value the build lane passes as --build-name (the one-version
+  #           scheme source: pubspec → tag → version job output, gh-785)
+  # approved: array of { "state" => ASC appStoreState, "version" => string }
+  # Returns a decision Hash:
+  #   { "action" => "abort", "floor" => "x.y.z", "reason" => why } — fail FAST, zero build minutes
+  #   { "action" => "pass",  "floor" => "x.y.z", "reason" => why }
+  def self.decide(stamped:, approved:)
+    floor = approved
+            .select { |v| APPROVED_STATES.include?(v["state"]) }
+            .map { |v| semver(v["version"]) }
+            .compact
+            .max || [0, 0, 0] # E2: first-ever release — trivially passable floor
+    stamped_v = semver(stamped)
+    if stamped_v.nil?
+      return decision("abort", floor, "stamped version #{stamped.inspect} is not a comparable x.y.z — the one-version scheme (gh-785) is broken")
+    end
+
+    if (stamped_v <=> floor) <= 0
+      return decision("abort", floor, "stamped #{stamped} ≤ approved #{floor.join('.')} — bump rule / one-version scheme broken (gh-785); refusing to spend build minutes on a guaranteed-rejected upload (iris 90062)")
+    end
+    decision("pass", floor, "stamped #{stamped} > approved #{floor.join('.')}")
+  end
+
+  # Strict x.y.z (minor/patch optional): nil for anything else, so garbage
+  # from ASC or the pipeline aborts named instead of comparing wrong.
+  def self.semver(string)
+    m = string.to_s.strip.match(/\A(\d+)(?:\.(\d+))?(?:\.(\d+))?\z/)
+    return nil unless m
+
+    [m[1].to_i, m[2].to_i, m[3].to_i]
+  end
+
+  def self.decision(action, floor, reason)
+    { "action" => action, "floor" => floor.join("."), "reason" => reason }
+  end
+end

build-ios:
    name: Build iOS IPA
    needs: version
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]
    # Issue #344: a wedged self-hosted worker (lost completion report)
    # otherwise holds the slot AND the in_progress status until the 300m
    # daily-publish watcher times out; a job-level timeout lets GitHub
    # fail the run server-side and unblock the pool + watchers.
    timeout-minutes: 90
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Update local git mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
          if [ ! -d "$MIRROR" ]; then
            git clone --mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
          else
            git -C "$MIRROR" fetch origin
          fi

      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C $GITHUB_WORKSPACE log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded
      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).
      - name: Setup Flutter (self-hosted)
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'

      - name: Setup environment (self-hosted)
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      # gh-798 AC1/AC2: fail FAST before any build minute is spent when the
      # version about to be stamped is not above ASC's approved floor
      # (#785's class: altool 90062 at the END of the build). Reads the
      # SAME version source the build lane stamps (BUILD_NAME of the
      # version job); the lane skips named without ASC secrets (the upload
      # leg skips too) and fails closed if ASC is unreachable (E1, one
      # retry). The AC4 marker line lands in the leg log either way.
      - name: Assert TestFlight version floor
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bundle install
          bundle exec fastlane ios assert_version_floor

      # Issue #726 (run 35491603044): pub re-fetches the moving `ref: master`
      # git deps (dart_git) on every resolve — pubspec.lock is untracked —
      # and one flaky TCP connect to github.com:443 ("Failed to connect
      # ... after 11155 ms") failed the whole leg with no retry. Bounded
      # retry with backoff; GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 fails fast on auth prompts
      # instead of hanging the self-hosted runner.
      - name: Install Flutter dependencies
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if flutter pub get; then
              exit 0
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::flutter pub get failed after 3 attempts — the runner's network to pub.dev/github.com is unhealthy"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::flutter pub get failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 15s"
            sleep 15
          done

      # The workspace is re-cloned every run, which wipes Pods/ and forces a
      # full pod install. Cache it keyed by the lockfile; $HOME-level caches
      # (pub-cache, CocoaPods download cache, Ruby gems, Flutter SDK) already
      # persist on the self-hosted runner.
      # v2: bust the cache — the Podfile.lock was stale (cupertino_http added
      # in 4bcac41 but the lockfile wasn't regenerated), so cached Pods were
      # missing the plugin's native code entirely. The build step's
      # `flutter build ios` runs `pod install` which regenerates the lockfile
      # with all registered plugins.
      - name: Cache CocoaPods (iOS)
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: flutter_app/ios/Pods
          key: ios-pods-v2-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/ios/Podfile.lock') }}

      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Prefer the local
          # working copy on this self-hosted runner; fall back to the upstream
          # release asset if the local copy is unavailable.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks"
          rm -rf "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "Local framework not found, downloading from upstream release..."
            # --retry alone skips transient mid-transfer resets (curl 56) —
            # the run-34709113737 failure: reset 3s into the 92.7 MB asset.
            curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
              -o /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip \
              https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip
            unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
          fi
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      - name: Validate iOS secrets

# Bounded wait for ASC processing (E1): external distribution needs a
# PROCESSED build — pilot silently SKIPS distribution when the wait is
# skipped. Default 90 min; override with TESTFLIGHT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.
def testflight_wait_timeout
  seconds = ENV["TESTFLIGHT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS"].to_i
  seconds.positive? ? seconds : 5400
end

def asc_token!
  require "spaceship"
  Spaceship::ConnectAPI.token ||= Spaceship::ConnectAPI::Token.create(
    key_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID"],
    issuer_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID"],
    key: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT"]
  )
end

def asc_app!(bundle_id:)
  require "spaceship"
  app = Spaceship::ConnectAPI::App.find(bundle_id)
  UI.user_error!("App #{bundle_id} not found in App Store Connect") if app.nil?
  app
end

# E3: pilot resolves groups BY NAME and silently skips adding the build when
# the name resolves to nothing — fail loudly instead, pointing at the
# variable. Returns [app, matched_group].
def find_external_testflight_group!(bundle_id:, group:)
  asc_token!
  app = asc_app!(bundle_id: bundle_id)
  found = app.get_beta_groups(includes: nil, limit: 200).select { |g| g.name == group }
  UI.user_error!("TestFlight external group '#{group}' (TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP) not found in App Store Connect — create it or fix the repo variable. Nothing was uploaded.") if found.empty?
  [app, found.first]
end

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.

## 1. ASC version-floor pre-check (testflight leg) — AC1/AC2/E1/E2/AC4

**Decision module** `flutter_app/fastlane/version_floor.rb` (the `appstore_preflight.rb` pattern: the lane fetches ASC facts, a dependency-free plain-ruby module decides → the whole matrix is testable without ASC):
- floor = max of **approved** versions only (`ACCEPTED` / `PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE` / `READY_FOR_SALE`) — in-review / TestFlight-only versions never raise it (they can still be rejected; the check must not block on them)
- `stamped ≤ floor` → named abort: *«stamped X ≤ approved Y — bump rule / one-version scheme broken (gh-785); refusing to spend build minutes on a guaranteed-rejected upload (iris 90062)»*
- **E2**: no approved versions → floor `0.0.0`, trivially passes, still markers
- garbage stamp → named abort instead of comparing wrong

**Wiring**: `build-mobile.yml` `build-ios` runs `fastlane ios assert_version_floor` as step 5 — before pub get (step 6), pods, certs, and the build (step 14): a violation costs **zero build minutes**. The lane reads the **same `BUILD_NAME` the build lane stamps** (`needs.version.outputs.version` — the pubspec → tag → version-job source #797 centralized).
- **E1**: ASC unreachable → exactly one retry, then fail-closed named error («cannot verify the version floor, refusing to build»)
- no ASC secrets → **named SKIP** (they're optional repo secrets; the upload leg skips too — nothing to guard), never silent
- **AC4**: the lane always logs `[gh-798] version-floor pre-check RAN: stamped=… approved_floor=… verdict=…` (and `SKIPPED` when skipping) — a silently-skipped check is visible in the daily report

**AC1/AC2 verified** by `flutter_app/fastlane/test/version_floor_test.rb` (10 checks, auto-picked-up by ci.yml's plain-ruby loop): AC1 below-floor abort incl. the exact #785 shape (`0.1.452` vs approved `1.0.0`), AC2 `1.0.453 > 1.0.452` passes, strict monotonicity (equal aborts), numeric compare (`1.0.9 ≤ 1.0.10`), E2, in-review-does-not-raise. Ran locally: `version_floor: 10 checks OK`.

- The gate moved out of build-mobile.yml into **`scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh`** — one source for the daily leg and the self-test, so they can't drift. Behavior byte-identical to #797's gate (same glob, same named verdict).

Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 800

- **Title**: ci(release): ASC version-floor pre-check + AAB gate self-test (#798)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/issue-798` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +398
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-09-22T08:39:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-22T19:20:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #798.

Both tripwires from the #797 triage, fail-closed, naming the rule each protects.

## 1. ASC version-floor pre-check (testflight leg) — AC1/AC2/E1/E2/AC4

**Decision module** `flutter_app/fastlane/version_floor.rb` (the `appstore_preflight.rb` pattern: the lane fetches ASC facts, a dependency-free plain-ruby module decides → the whole matrix is testable without ASC):
- floor = max of **approved** versions only (`ACCEPTED` / `PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE` / `READY_FOR_SALE`) — in-review / TestFlight-only versions never raise it (they can still be rejected; the check must not block on them)
- `stamped ≤ floor` → named abort: *«stamped X ≤ approved Y — bump rule / one-version scheme broken (gh-785); refusing to spend build minutes on a guaranteed-rejected upload (iris 90062)»*
- **E2**: no approved versions → floor `0.0.0`, trivially passes, still markers
- garbage stamp → named abort instead of comparing wrong

**Wiring**: `build-mobile.yml` `build-ios` runs `fastlane ios assert_version_floor` as step 5 — before pub get (step 6), pods, certs, and the build (step 14): a violation costs **zero build minutes**. The lane reads the **same `BUILD_NAME` the build lane stamps** (`needs.version.outputs.version` — the pubspec → tag → version-job source #797 centralized).
- **E1**: ASC unreachable → exactly one retry, then fail-closed named error («cannot verify the version floor, refusing to build»)
- no ASC secrets → **named SKIP** (they're optional repo secrets; the upload leg skips too — nothing to guard), never silent
- **AC4**: the lane always logs `[gh-798] version-floor pre-check RAN: stamped=… approved_floor=… verdict=…` (and `SKIPPED` when skipping) — a silently-skipped check is visible in the daily report

**AC1/AC2 verified** by `flutter_app/fastlane/test/version_floor_test.rb` (10 checks, auto-picked-up by ci.yml's plain-ruby loop): AC1 below-floor abort incl. the exact #785 shape (`0.1.452` vs approved `1.0.0`), AC2 `1.0.453 > 1.0.452` passes, strict monotonicity (equal aborts), numeric compare (`1.0.9 ≤ 1.0.10`), E2, in-review-does-not-raise. Ran locally: `version_floor: 10 checks OK`.

## 2. AAB 16 KB-gate self-test — AC3/E3

- The gate moved out of build-mobile.yml into **`scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh`** — one source for the daily leg and the self-test, so they can't drift. Behavior byte-identical to #797's gate (same glob, same named verdict).
- **`.github/workflows/aab-gate-selftest.yml`**: PR-triggered on the workflow / gate script / checker paths (+ manual dispatch). Builds two fixtures and runs the **real script**:
  - (a) real 16 KB-aligned vendored `.so` at `base/lib/<abi>/` (AAB layout) → gate passes **and** the green marker must be present
  - (b) lib-less bundle → gate must fail **and** output must contain the named `::error:: expected native libs at base/lib/*/*.so …` verdict — catching a regression to an inherited/unlabeled exit code (the exact gh-786 class)
- The fixture is AAB-layout, so **any glob/layout regression fails case (a) red** — demonstrated locally: sed-regressing the glob back to `lib/*` makes the with-libs fixture fail with the named error.

# pr-800: ci(release): ASC version-floor pre-check + AAB gate self-test (#798)

## Description

Closes #798.

Both tripwires from the #797 triage, fail-closed, naming the rule each protects.

## 1. ASC version-floor pre-check (testflight leg) — AC1/AC2/E1/E2/AC4

**Decision module** `flutter_app/fastlane/version_floor.rb` (the `appstore_preflight.rb` pattern: the lane fetches ASC facts, a dependency-free plain-ruby module decides → the whole matrix is testable without ASC):
- floor = max of **approved** versions only (`ACCEPTED` / `PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE` / `READY_FOR_SALE`) — in-review / TestFlight-only versions never raise it (they can still be rejected; the check must not block on them)
- `stamped ≤ floor` → named abort: *«stamped X ≤ approved Y — bump rule / one-version scheme broken (gh-785); refusing to spend build minutes on a guaranteed-rejected upload (iris 90062)»*
- **E2**: no approved versions → floor `0.0.0`, trivially passes, still markers
- garbage stamp → named abort instead of comparing wrong

**Wiring**: `build-mobile.yml` `build-ios` runs `fastlane ios assert_version_floor` as step 5 — before pub get (step 6), pods, certs, and the build (step 14): a violation costs **zero build minutes**. The lane reads the **same `BUILD_NAME` the build lane stamps** (`needs.version.outputs.version` — the pubspec → tag → version-job source #797 centralized).
- **E1**: ASC unreachable → exactly one retry, then fail-closed named error («cannot verify the version floor, refusing to build»)
- no ASC secrets → **named SKIP** (they're optional repo secrets; the upload leg skips too — nothing to guard), never silent
- **AC4**: the lane always logs `[gh-798] version-floor pre-check RAN: stamped=… approved_floor=… verdict=…` (and `SKIPPED` when skipping) — a silently-skipped check is visible in the daily report

**AC1/AC2 verified** by `flutter_app/fastlane/test/version_floor_test.rb` (10 checks, auto-picked-up by ci.yml's plain-ruby loop): AC1 below-floor abort incl. the exact #785 shape (`0.1.452` vs approved `1.0.0`), AC2 `1.0.453 > 1.0.452` passes, strict monotonicity (equal aborts), numeric compare (`1.0.9 ≤ 1.0.10`), E2, in-review-does-not-raise. +  raise "FAIL: garbage stamp must abort named, got #{d.inspect}" unless d["action"] == "abort" && d["reason"].include?("not a comparable")

index 00000000..6fc37521
--- /dev/null
+++ b/flutter_app/fastlane/version_floor.rb
@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+# frozen_string_literal: true
+
+# Pure decision logic for the TestFlight version-floor pre-check (issue
+# #798, triage of #785): the daily leg must abort BEFORE any build when the
+# version it is about to stamp is not strictly above the latest version App
+# Store Connect has already APPROVED (iris-code 90062 — a 20-minute build
+# ending in altool rejection is the failure class this kills). Dependency-
+# free — no fastlane/spaceship requires: the Fastfile lane fetches the ASC
+# facts, this module decides, so the whole matrix is testable with plain
+# ruby (test/version_floor_test.rb — no gems needed).
+module VersionFloor
+  # App Store states where Apple has APPROVED the version — only these
+  # raise the floor Apple's monotonicity check (90062) compares against.
+  # A version that merely exists as a TestFlight build or sits in review
+  # never counts: it can still be rejected, and the check must not block
+  # on it.
+  APPROVED_STATES = %w[
+    ACCEPTED
+    PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE
+    READY_FOR_SALE
+  ].freeze
+
+  # stamped:  the version the leg is about to stamp — BUILD_NAME, the same
+  #           value the build lane passes as --build-name (the one-version
+  #           scheme source: pubspec → tag → version job output, gh-785)
+  # approved: array of { "state" => ASC appStoreState, "version" => string }
+  # Returns a decision Hash:
+  #   { "action" => "abort", "floor" => "x.y.z", "reason" => why } — fail FAST, zero build minutes
+  #   { "action" => "pass",  "floor" => "x.y.z", "reason" => why }
+  def self.decide(stamped:, approved:)
+    floor = approved
+            .select { |v| APPROVED_STATES.include?(v["state"]) }
+            .map { |v| semver(v["version"]) }
+            .compact
+            .max || [0, 0, 0] # E2: first-ever release — trivially passable floor
+    stamped_v = semver(stamped)
+    if stamped_v.nil?
+      return decision("abort", floor, "stamped version #{stamped.inspect} is not a comparable x.y.z — the one-version scheme (gh-785) is broken")
+    end
+
+    if (stamped_v <=> floor) <= 0
+      return decision("abort", floor, "stamped #{stamped} ≤ approved #{floor.join('.')} — bump rule / one-version scheme broken (gh-785); refusing to spend build minutes on a guaranteed-rejected upload (iris 90062)")
+    end
+    decision("pass", floor, "stamped #{stamped} > approved #{floor.join('.')}")
+  end
+
+  # Strict x.y.z (minor/patch optional): nil for anything else, so garbage
+  # from ASC or the pipeline aborts named instead of comparing wrong.
+  def self.semver(string)
+    m = string.to_s.strip.match(/\A(\d+)(?:\.(\d+))?(?:\.(\d+))?\z/)
+    return nil unless m
+
+    [m[1].to_i, m[2].to_i, m[3].to_i]
+  end
+
+  def self.decision(action, floor, reason)
+    { "action" => action, "floor" => floor.join("."), "reason" => reason }
+  end
+end

build-ios:
    name: Build iOS IPA
    needs: version
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]
    # Issue #344: a wedged self-hosted worker (lost completion report)
    # otherwise holds the slot AND the in_progress status until the 300m
    # daily-publish watcher times out; a job-level timeout lets GitHub
    # fail the run server-side and unblock the pool + watchers.
    timeout-minutes: 90
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Update local git mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
          if [ ! -d "$MIRROR" ]; then
            git clone --mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
          else
            git -C "$MIRROR" fetch origin
          fi

      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C $GITHUB_WORKSPACE log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded
      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).
      - name: Setup Flutter (self-hosted)
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'

      - name: Setup environment (self-hosted)
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      # gh-798 AC1/AC2: fail FAST before any build minute is spent when the
      # version about to be stamped is not above ASC's approved floor
      # (#785's class: altool 90062 at the END of the build). Reads the
      # SAME version source the build lane stamps (BUILD_NAME of the
      # version job); the lane skips named without ASC secrets (the upload
      # leg skips too) and fails closed if ASC is unreachable (E1, one
      # retry). The AC4 marker line lands in the leg log either way.
      - name: Assert TestFlight version floor
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bundle install
          bundle exec fastlane ios assert_version_floor

      # Issue #726 (run 35491603044): pub re-fetches the moving `ref: master`
      # git deps (dart_git) on every resolve — pubspec.lock is untracked —
      # and one flaky TCP connect to github.com:443 ("Failed to connect
      # ... after 11155 ms") failed the whole leg with no retry. Bounded
      # retry with backoff; GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 fails fast on auth prompts
      # instead of hanging the self-hosted runner.
      - name: Install Flutter dependencies
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if flutter pub get; then
              exit 0
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::flutter pub get failed after 3 attempts — the runner's network to pub.dev/github.com is unhealthy"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::flutter pub get failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 15s"
            sleep 15
          done

      # The workspace is re-cloned every run, which wipes Pods/ and forces a
      # full pod install. Cache it keyed by the lockfile; $HOME-level caches
      # (pub-cache, CocoaPods download cache, Ruby gems, Flutter SDK) already
      # persist on the self-hosted runner.
      # v2: bust the cache — the Podfile.lock was stale (cupertino_http added
      # in 4bcac41 but the lockfile wasn't regenerated), so cached Pods were
      # missing the plugin's native code entirely. The build step's
      # `flutter build ios` runs `pod install` which regenerates the lockfile
      # with all registered plugins.
      - name: Cache CocoaPods (iOS)
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: flutter_app/ios/Pods
          key: ios-pods-v2-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/ios/Podfile.lock') }}

      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Prefer the local
          # working copy on this self-hosted runner; fall back to the upstream
          # release asset if the local copy is unavailable.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks"
          rm -rf "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"

# Bounded wait for ASC processing (E1): external distribution needs a
# PROCESSED build — pilot silently SKIPS distribution when the wait is
# skipped. Default 90 min; override with TESTFLIGHT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.
def testflight_wait_timeout
  seconds = ENV["TESTFLIGHT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS"].to_i
  seconds.positive? ? seconds : 5400
end

def asc_token!
  require "spaceship"
  Spaceship::ConnectAPI.token ||= Spaceship::ConnectAPI::Token.create(
    key_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID"],
    issuer_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID"],
    key: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT"]
  )
end

def asc_app!(bundle_id:)
  require "spaceship"
  app = Spaceship::ConnectAPI::App.find(bundle_id)
  UI.user_error!("App #{bundle_id} not found in App Store Connect") if app.nil?
  app
end

# E3: pilot resolves groups BY NAME and silently skips adding the build when
# the name resolves to nothing — fail loudly instead, pointing at the
# variable. Returns [app, matched_group].
def find_external_testflight_group!(bundle_id:, group:)
  asc_token!
  app = asc_app!(bundle_id: bundle_id)
  found = app.get_beta_groups(includes: nil, limit: 200).select { |g| g.name == group }
  UI.user_error!("TestFlight external group '#{group}' (TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP) not found in App Store Connect — create it or fix the repo variable. Nothing was uploaded.") if found.empty?
  [app, found.first]
end

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.

## 1. ASC version-floor pre-check (testflight leg) — AC1/AC2/E1/E2/AC4

**Decision module** `flutter_app/fastlane/version_floor.rb` (the `appstore_preflight.rb` pattern: the lane fetches ASC facts, a dependency-free plain-ruby module decides → the whole matrix is testable without ASC):
- floor = max of **approved** versions only (`ACCEPTED` / `PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE` / `READY_FOR_SALE`) — in-review / TestFlight-only versions never raise it (they can still be rejected; the check must not block on them)
- `stamped ≤ floor` → named abort: *«stamped X ≤ approved Y — bump rule / one-version scheme broken (gh-785); refusing to spend build minutes on a guaranteed-rejected upload (iris 90062)»*
- **E2**: no approved versions → floor `0.0.0`, trivially passes, still markers
- garbage stamp → named abort instead of comparing wrong

**Wiring**: `build-mobile.yml` `build-ios` runs `fastlane ios assert_version_floor` as step 5 — before pub get (step 6), pods, certs, and the build (step 14): a violation costs **zero build minutes**. The lane reads the **same `BUILD_NAME` the build lane stamps** (`needs.version.outputs.version` — the pubspec → tag → version-job source #797 centralized).
- **E1**: ASC unreachable → exactly one retry, then fail-closed named error («cannot verify the version floor, refusing to build»)
- no ASC secrets → **named SKIP** (they're optional repo secrets; the upload leg skips too — nothing to guard), never silent
- **AC4**: the lane always logs `[gh-798] version-floor pre-check RAN: stamped=… approved_floor=… verdict=…` (and `SKIPPED` when skipping) — a silently-skipped check is visible in the daily report

**AC1/AC2 verified** by `flutter_app/fastlane/test/version_floor_test.rb` (10 checks, auto-picked-up by ci.yml's plain-ruby loop): AC1 below-floor abort incl. the exact #785 shape (`0.1.452` vs approved `1.0.0`), AC2 `1.0.453 > 1.0.452` passes, strict monotonicity (equal aborts), numeric compare (`1.0.9 ≤ 1.0.10`), E2, in-review-does-not-raise. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 800
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/800
- **Title**: ci(release): ASC version-floor pre-check + AAB gate self-test (#798)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/issue-798` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +398
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-09-22T08:39:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-22T19:20:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #798.

Both tripwires from the #797 triage, fail-closed, naming the rule each protects.

## 1. ASC version-floor pre-check (testflight leg) — AC1/AC2/E1/E2/AC4

**Decision module** `flutter_app/fastlane/version_floor.rb` (the `appstore_preflight.rb` pattern: the lane fetches ASC facts, a dependency-free plain-ruby module decides → the whole matrix is testable without ASC):
- floor = max of **approved** versions only (`ACCEPTED` / `PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE` / `READY_FOR_SALE`) — in-review / TestFlight-only versions never raise it (they can still be rejected; the check must not block on them)
- `stamped ≤ floor` → named abort: *«stamped X ≤ approved Y — bump rule / one-version scheme broken (gh-785); refusing to spend build minutes on a guaranteed-rejected upload (iris 90062)»*
- **E2**: no approved versions → floor `0.0.0`, trivially passes, still markers
- garbage stamp → named abort instead of comparing wrong

**Wiring**: `build-mobile.yml` `build-ios` runs `fastlane ios assert_version_floor` as step 5 — before pub get (step 6), pods, certs, and the build (step 14): a violation costs **zero build minutes**. The lane reads the **same `BUILD_NAME` the build lane stamps** (`needs.version.outputs.version` — the pubspec → tag → version-job source #797 centralized).
- **E1**: ASC unreachable → exactly one retry, then fail-closed named error («cannot verify the version floor, refusing to build»)
- no ASC secrets → **named SKIP** (they're optional repo secrets; the upload leg skips too — nothing to guard), never silent
- **AC4**: the lane always logs `[gh-798] version-floor pre-check RAN: stamped=… approved_floor=… verdict=…` (and `SKIPPED` when skipping) — a silently-skipped check is visible in the daily report

**AC1/AC2 verified** by `flutter_app/fastlane/test/version_floor_test.rb` (10 checks, auto-picked-up by ci.yml's plain-ruby loop): AC1 below-floor abort incl. the exact #785 shape (`0.1.452` vs approved `1.0.0`), AC2 `1.0.453 > 1.0.452` passes, strict monotonicity (equal aborts), numeric compare (`1.0.9 ≤ 1.0.10`), E2, in-review-does-not-raise. Ran locally: `version_floor: 10 checks OK`.

## 2. AAB 16 KB-gate self-test — AC3/E3

- The gate moved out of build-mobile.yml into **`scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh`** — one source for the daily leg and the self-test, so they can't drift. Behavior byte-identical to #797's gate (same glob, same named verdict).
- **`.github/workflows/aab-gate-selftest.yml`**: PR-triggered on the workflow / gate script / checker paths (+ manual dispatch). Builds two fixtures and runs the **real script**:
  - (a) real 16 KB-aligned vendored `.so` at `base/lib/<abi>/` (AAB layout) → gate passes **and** the green marker must be present
  - (b) lib-less bundle → gate must fail **and** output must contain the named `::error:: expected native libs at base/lib/*/*.so …` verdict — catching a regression to an inherited/unlabeled exit code (the exact gh-786 class)
- The fixture is AAB-layout, so **any glob/layout regression fails case (a) red** — demonstrated locally: sed-regressing the glob back to `lib/*` makes the with-libs fixture fail with the named error.
- Local run against the fixtures: (a) `scanned 1, patched 0, failed 0` + green; (b) named failure, exit 1.

## Guards

`test/store_automation_guard_test.dart` gains a `release-train tripwires (gh-798)` group: floor step must stay **before** build prep in build-ios, the lane must keep using the tested module + the AC4 marker, the daily gate must run via the shared script, and the self-test workflow must trigger on gate-script PRs. (The dart guard suite couldn't run in this sandbox — pub cache is denied — so the pinned facts were verified with an equivalent ruby check; the suite runs in CI.)

**Non-goals respected:** the `1.0.<counter>` scheme itself is untouched; no release automation beyond the two tripwires.

+name: AAB 16k gate self-test

+# gh-798 AC3: the 16 KB page-size gate (scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh,
+# called by build-mobile.yml's "Verify AAB" step) is itself tested — a gate
+# that is wrong from day one (gh-786: APK-layout glob in an AAB) must be
+# caught at PR time, not by the nightly. This job runs the REAL gate script
+# against two fixture bundles:
+#   (a) libs present (a real 16 KB-aligned vendored .so under the AAB
+#       layout base/lib/<abi>/) → gate passes with the green marker;
+#   (b) libs absent → the named "::error:: expected native libs …"
+#       verdict, never a silent pass, never an inherited exit code.
+# A regressed glob or verdict turns this job red and blocks merge — the
+# fixture is the AAB layout, so ANY layout assumption regression fails
+# case (a) exactly like the nightly did (gh-786). A failure on an
+# unrelated change is the desired loudness — fix the gate or fixture,
+# never delete the job (gh-798 E3).
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    paths:
+      - '.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml'
+      - '.github/workflows/aab-gate-selftest.yml'

+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:

+    name: Gate self-test (fixture bundles)
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 15
+    steps:

+        uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2

+

+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail

+          mkdir -p fx/with-libs/base/lib/arm64-v8a

+          (cd fx/with-libs && zip -q -r -X ../with-libs.aab base)
+          # (b) without libs: structurally valid bundle, zero native libs.
+          mkdir -p fx/without-libs/base
+          (cd fx/without-libs && zip -q -r -X ../without-libs.aab base)

+
+      - name: "(a) libs present → gate passes"
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          OUT="$(mktemp)"
+          if bash scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh fx/with-libs.aab >"$OUT" 2>&1; then

+            exit 1
+          }
+          echo "✅ self-test green: pass-on-libs + named-fail-without-libs verified"

+# frozen_string_literal: true
+
+# Issue #798 AC1/AC2/E2 — the TestFlight version-floor pre-check matrix.
+# Plain ruby, no gems (runs on the CI runner's stock ruby and anywhere
+# else):
+#
+#   ruby flutter_app/fastlane/test/version_floor_test.rb
+#
+# Guarded by $PROGRAM_NAME so an accidental require by fastlane's loader
+# never executes the checks.
+
+require_relative "../version_floor"
+
+if $PROGRAM_NAME == __FILE__
+  $checks = 0
+
+  def ok(message)
+    $checks += 1
+    puts "  ok: #{message}"
+  end
+
+  def approved(version, state = "READY_FOR_SALE")
+    { "state" => state, "version" => version }
+  end
+
+  # AC1 — stamped below the approved floor → named abort, zero build minutes
+  d = VersionFloor.decide(stamped: "1.0.100", approved: [approved("1.0.452")])
+  raise "FAIL: below-floor must abort, got #{d.inspect}" unless d["action"] == "abort" && d["floor"] == "1.0.452" && d["reason"].include?("stamped 1.0.100 ≤ approved 1.0.452") && d["reason"].include?("gh-785")
+  ok("AC1: stamped 1.0.100 ≤ approved 1.0.452 → named abort")
+
+  # AC1 as it happened in #785 — the 0.1.x train under an approved 1.0.0
+  d = VersionFloor.decide(stamped: "0.1.452", approved: [approved("1.0.0")])
+  raise "FAIL: #785 shape must abort, got #{d.inspect}" unless d["action"] == "abort" && d["reason"].include?("0.1.452 ≤ approved 1.0.0")
+  ok("AC1: the #785 shape (0.1.452 vs approved 1.0.0) aborts")
+
+  # AC2 — stamped above the floor → pass
+  d = VersionFloor.decide(stamped: "1.0.453", approved: [approved("1.0.452")])
+  raise "FAIL: above-floor must pass, got #{d.inspect}" unless d["action"] == "pass" && d["reason"].include?("stamped 1.0.453 > approved 1.0.452")
+  ok("AC2: stamped 1.0.453 > approved 1.0.452 → pass")
+
+  # Equal version is NOT above the floor (90062 is a strict monotonicity)
+  d = VersionFloor.decide(stamped: "1.0.452", approved: [approved("1.0.452")])
+  raise "FAIL: equal must abort, got #{d.inspect}" unless d["action"] == "abort"
+  ok("equal stamped == approved → abort (strict monotonicity)")
+
+  # E2 — first-ever release: no approved versions → floor 0.0.0, passes
+  d = VersionFloor.decide(stamped: "1.0.1", approved: [])
+  raise "FAIL: empty approved must pass with floor 0.0.0, got #{d.inspect}" unless d["action"] == "pass" && d["floor"] == "0.0.0"
+  ok("E2: no approved versions → floor 0.0.0, trivially passes")
+
+  # E2 marker stays meaningful — the floor is surfaced either way
+  d = VersionFloor.decide(stamped: "1.0.1", approved: [approved("0.9.9", "REJECTED")])
+  raise "FAIL: rejected versions must not raise the floor, got #{d.inspect}" unless d["action"] == "pass" && d["floor"] == "0.0.0"
+  ok("REJECTED versions never raise the floor")
+
+  # Only genuinely approved states raise the floor: a TestFlight-only
+  # version (no App Store entry) or one still in review does not block.
+  d = VersionFloor.decide(
+    stamped: "1.0.5",
+    approved: [
+      approved("1.0.4", "READY_FOR_SALE"),
+      approved("1.0.9", "WAITING_FOR_REVIEW"),
+      approved("1.0.8", "IN_REVIEW"),
+      { "state" => "READY_FOR_SALE", "version" => "not-a-version" }
+    ]
+  )
+  raise "FAIL: in-review entries must not raise the floor, got #{d.inspect}" unless d["action"] == "pass" && d["floor"] == "1.0.4"
+  ok("floor = max of APPROVED states only; in-review (1.0.9/1.0.8)/garbage entries ignored")
+
+  # All three approved states count (ACCEPTED and pending-dev-release are

+  raise "FAIL: ACCEPTED must raise the floor, got #{d.inspect}" unless d["action"] == "pass" && d["floor"] == "1.0.8"
+  ok("ACCEPTED/PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE count as approved")
+
+  # Numeric comparison, not string: 1.0.9 < 1.0.10

+  raise "FAIL: numeric compare broken, got #{d.inspect}" unless d["action"] == "abort" && d["floor"] == "1.0.10"
+  ok("numeric compare: 1.0.9 ≤ 1.0.10 aborts")

+  raise "FAIL: garbage stamp must abort named, got #{d.inspect}" unless d["action"] == "abort" && d["reason"].include?("not a comparable")
+  ok("garbage stamp → named abort")
+

+end

+# frozen_string_literal: true
+
+# Pure decision logic for the TestFlight version-floor pre-check (issue
+# #798, triage of #785): the daily leg must abort BEFORE any build when the
+# version it is about to stamp is not strictly above the latest version App
+# Store Connect has already APPROVED (iris-code 90062 — a 20-minute build
+# ending in altool rejection is the failure class this kills). Dependency-
+# free — no fastlane/spaceship requires: the Fastfile lane fetches the ASC
+# facts, this module decides, so the whole matrix is testable with plain
+# ruby (test/version_floor_test.rb — no gems needed).
+module VersionFloor
+  # App Store states where Apple has APPROVED the version — only these
+  # raise the floor Apple's monotonicity check (90062) compares against.
+  # A version that merely exists as a TestFlight build or sits in review
+  # never counts: it can still be rejected, and the check must not block
+  # on it.
+  APPROVED_STATES = %w[
+    ACCEPTED
+    PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE
+    READY_FOR_SALE
+  ].freeze
+
+  # stamped:  the version the leg is about to stamp — BUILD_NAME, the same
+  #           value the build lane passes as --build-name (the one-version
+  #           scheme source: pubspec → tag → version job output, gh-785)
+  # approved: array of { "state" => ASC appStoreState, "version" => string }
+  # Returns a decision Hash:
+  #   { "action" => "abort", "floor" => "x.y.z", "reason" => why } — fail FAST, zero build minutes
+  #   { "action" => "pass",  "floor" => "x.y.z", "reason" => why }
+  def self.decide(stamped:, approved:)
+    floor = approved
+            .select { |v| APPROVED_STATES.include?(v["state"]) }
+            .map { |v| semver(v["version"]) }
+            .compact
+            .max || [0, 0, 0] # E2: first-ever release — trivially passable floor
+    stamped_v = semver(stamped)
+    if stamped_v.nil?
+      return decision("abort", floor, "stamped version #{stamped.inspect} is not a comparable x.y.z — the one-version scheme (gh-785) is broken")
+    end
+
+    if (stamped_v <=> floor) <= 0
+      return decision("abort", floor, "stamped #{stamped} ≤ approved #{floor.join('.')} — bump rule / one-version scheme broken (gh-785); refusing to spend build minutes on a guaranteed-rejected upload (iris 90062)")
+    end
+    decision("pass", floor, "stamped #{stamped} > approved #{floor.join('.')}")
+  end
+
+  # Strict x.y.z (minor/patch optional): nil for anything else, so garbage
+  # from ASC or the pipeline aborts named instead of comparing wrong.
+  def self.semver(string)
+    m = string.to_s.strip.match(/\A(\d+)(?:\.(\d+))?(?:\.(\d+))?\z/)
+    return nil unless m
+
+    [m[1].to_i, m[2].to_i, m[3].to_i]
+  end
+
+  def self.decision(action, floor, reason)
+    { "action" => action, "floor" => floor.join("."), "reason" => reason }
+  end
+end

    # Issue #344: a wedged self-hosted worker (lost completion report)

# Bounded wait for ASC processing (E1): external distribution needs a
# PROCESSED build — pilot silently SKIPS distribution when the wait is
# skipped. Default 90 min; override with TESTFLIGHT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.
def testflight_wait_timeout
  seconds = ENV["TESTFLIGHT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS"].to_i
  seconds.positive? ? seconds : 5400
end

def asc_token!
  require "spaceship"
  Spaceship::ConnectAPI.token ||= Spaceship::ConnectAPI::Token.create(
    key_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID"],
    issuer_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID"],
    key: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT"]
  )
end

def asc_app!(bundle_id:)
  require "spaceship"
  app = Spaceship::ConnectAPI::App.find(bundle_id)
  UI.user_error!("App #{bundle_id} not found in App Store Connect") if app.nil?
  app
end

# E3: pilot resolves groups BY NAME and silently skips adding the build when
# the name resolves to nothing — fail loudly instead, pointing at the
# variable. Returns [app, matched_group].
def find_external_testflight_group!(bundle_id:, group:)
  asc_token!
  app = asc_app!(bundle_id: bundle_id)
  found = app.get_beta_groups(includes: nil, limit: 200).select { |g| g.name == group }
  UI.user_error!("TestFlight external group '#{group}' (TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP) not found in App Store Connect — create it or fix the repo variable. Nothing was uploaded.") if found.empty?
  [app, found.first]
end

Minor documentation mismatch — SUGGESTION.

F. Version-floor lane is in `platform :ios` — invoked via `bundle exec fastlane ios assert_version_floor` from build-ios. OK.

G. The pre-check step env: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID`/`ISSUER_ID` may be empty while KEY_CONTENT is set — asc_token! would fail with cryptic error → E1 fail-closed path names it "unreachable after one retry" — message slightly misleading but fail-closed nonetheless. Fine.

H. The retry: `retry if tries < 2` — but `retry` in a `begin/rescue` retries from the top of begin. `tries += 1` → second pass tries=2. On second failure: `retry if tries < 2` false → user_error. Exactly one retry as documented. Good. But one subtlety: `UI.user_error!` raises FastlaneCore::Interface::FastlaneError which is a StandardError subclass? Actually FastlaneError < StandardError. If `asc_app!` calls `UI.user_error!("App not found...")` — that raise happens INSIDE the begin block → rescue StandardError catches it → retries once → fails again → the rescue then reports "App Store Connect unreachable after one retry (...)" with FastlaneError message "App dev.fa1.app not found in App Store Connect". The named "app not found" error gets re-wrapped into a misleading "ASC unreachable" error. Hmm — that's a real (minor) issue: `UI.user_error!` inside the begin is rescued and misreported as unreachability. Also — worse: retrying on a user_error ("app not found") wastes one retry and produces a confusing message, but it still fails closed. Severity: SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? It's a diagnostics-quality issue, not correctness of the gate (still fails closed, named-ish message includes the underlying message). I'd rate SUGGESTION. Actually wait — there's something more subtle: does `UI.user_error!` get caught by `rescue StandardError`? FastlaneCore::Interface::FastlaneError inherits from StandardError — yes. So an app-not-found produces "version-floor pre-check: App Store Connect unreachable after one retry (FastlaneCore::Interface::FastlaneError: App dev.fa1.app not found in App Store Connect) — failing closed". Retrying a deterministic error is wasteful but bounded (one retry, seconds). Message still informative enough (contains the real reason). SUGGESTION.

I. Version floor compares only against `get_app_store_versions` (App Store versions) — per design.

J. `semver` allows "1" or "1.2" (minor/patch optional) — stamped "auto"? The version job outputs e.g. "0.1.446". BUILD_NAME="auto"? K. In `version_floor.rb`, `floor` array max: arrays of different lengths? semver always returns 3-element arrays. OK.

L. The `.max` on arrays compares lexicographically — [1,0,452] vs [1,1,0]: element-wise numeric. Correct.

N. Guard test uses `expect(names.indexOf(...), lessThan(names.indexOf('Install Flutter dependencies')))` — both exist. That's acceptable guard behavior (renames should be caught)... actually if 'Assert TestFlight version floor' were REMOVED, indexOf → -1 < index → -1 < 6 → TRUE → test PASSES even though the step is gone! # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.

      - name: Setup Ruby
        # ubuntu-24.04 runner images ship no Ruby — `bundle: command not
        # found` exit 127 (issue #353). Same setup as store-metadata.yml.
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'

      - name: Install fastlane
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: bundle install

      # The lane wraps `flutter build appbundle --release`; the upload
      # keystore rides the ANDROID_* env vars (issue #289) and is decoded
      # by app/build.gradle.kts into the (gitignored) build dir — no
      # key.properties dance. ANDROID_STRICT_RELEASE_SIGNING makes a
      # secret-less release build fail LOUDLY instead of debug-signing.
      - name: Build Android AAB
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          ANDROID_STRICT_RELEASE_SIGNING: 'true'
        run: bundle exec fastlane android build_release

      - name: Verify AAB and validate bundle
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          AAB_PATH="flutter_app/build/app/outputs/bundle/storeRelease/app-store-release.aab"
          if [ ! -f "$AAB_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::AAB file not found at $AAB_PATH"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "AAB built successfully: $(ls -la $AAB_PATH)"
          # bundletool validate (issue #289 AC3): catches malformed bundles
          # before they ever reach Play's upload pipeline.
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o /tmp/bundletool.jar \
            https://github.com/google/bundletool/releases/download/1.17.0/bundletool-all-1.17.0.jar
          java -jar /tmp/bundletool.jar validate --bundle "$AAB_PATH"

Both tripwires from the #797 triage, fail-closed, naming the rule each protects.

## 1. ASC version-floor pre-check (testflight leg) — AC1/AC2/E1/E2/AC4

**Decision module** `flutter_app/fastlane/version_floor.rb` (the `appstore_preflight.rb` pattern: the lane fetches ASC facts, a dependency-free plain-ruby module decides → the whole matrix is testable without ASC):
- floor = max of **approved** versions only (`ACCEPTED` / `PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE` / `READY_FOR_SALE`) — in-review / TestFlight-only versions never raise it (they can still be rejected; the check must not block on them)
- `stamped ≤ floor` → named abort: *«stamped X ≤ approved Y — bump rule / one-version scheme broken (gh-785); refusing to spend build minutes on a guaranteed-rejected upload (iris 90062)»*
- **E2**: no approved versions → floor `0.0.0`, trivially passes, still markers
- garbage stamp → named abort instead of comparing wrong

**Wiring**: `build-mobile.yml` `build-ios` runs `fastlane ios assert_version_floor` as step 5 — before pub get (step 6), pods, certs, and the build (step 14): a violation costs **zero build minutes**. The lane reads the **same `BUILD_NAME` the build lane stamps** (`needs.version.outputs.version` — the pubspec → tag → version-job source #797 centralized).
- **E1**: ASC unreachable → exactly one retry, then fail-closed named error («cannot verify the version floor, refusing to build»)
- no ASC secrets → **named SKIP** (they're optional repo secrets; the upload leg skips too — nothing to guard), never silent
- **AC4**: the lane always logs `[gh-798] version-floor pre-check RAN: stamped=… approved_floor=… verdict=…` (and `SKIPPED` when skipping) — a silently-skipped check is visible in the daily report

**AC1/AC2 verified** by `flutter_app/fastlane/test/version_floor_test.rb` (10 checks, auto-picked-up by ci.yml's plain-ruby loop): AC1 below-floor abort incl. the exact #785 shape (`0.1.452` vs approved `1.0.0`), AC2 `1.0.453 > 1.0.452` passes, strict monotonicity (equal aborts), numeric compare (`1.0.9 ≤ 1.0.10`), E2, in-review-does-not-raise. Ran locally: `version_floor: 10 checks OK`.

## 2. AAB 16 KB-gate self-test — AC3/E3

- The gate moved out of build-mobile.yml into **`scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh`** — one source for the daily leg and the self-test, so they can't drift. Behavior byte-identical to #797's gate (same glob, same named verdict).
- **`.github/workflows/aab-gate-selftest.yml`**: PR-triggered on the workflow / gate script / checker paths (+ manual dispatch). Builds two fixtures and runs the **real script**:
  - (a) real 16 KB-aligned vendored `.so` at `base/lib/<abi>/` (AAB layout) → gate passes **and** the green marker must be present
  - (b) lib-less bundle → gate must fail **and** output must contain the named `::error:: expected native libs at base/lib/*/*.so …` verdict — catching a regression to an inherited/unlabeled exit code (the exact gh-786 class)
- The fixture is AAB-layout, so **any glob/layout regression fails case (a) red** — demonstrated locally: sed-regressing the glob back to `lib/*` makes the with-libs fixture fail with the named error.
- Local run against the fixtures: (a) `scanned 1, patched 0, failed 0` + green; (b) named failure, exit 1.

## Guards

`test/store_automation_guard_test.dart` gains a `release-train tripwires (gh-798)` group: floor step must stay **before** build prep in build-ios, the lane must keep using the tested module + the AC4 marker, the daily gate must run via the shared script, and the self-test workflow must trigger on gate-script PRs. (The dart guard suite couldn't run in this sandbox — pub cache is denied — so the pinned facts were verified with an equivalent ruby check; the suite runs in CI.)

**Non-goals respected:** the `1.0.<counter>` scheme itself is untouched; no release automation beyond the two tripwires."
